subject: general
question: What will be the simple interest on a sum of Rs. 12000 at the rate of 15 percent per annum for three years ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total interest percentage for 3 years = Rate × Time = 15% × 3 = 45%.

Simple Interest = 45% of ₹12,000.

SI = (45 ÷ 100) × 12,000 = 45 × 120 = ₹5400.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Principal (P) = ₹12,000, Rate (R) = 15%, Time (T) = 3 years.

Formula: Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9897743c3a3a6a751354fb7a7213a37842c6d4b5afbdea433f726887155db7c9.png] 

⇒ SI = (12000 × 15 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 120 × 15 × 3

⇒ SI = 1800 × 3

⇒ SI = ₹5400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The total amount (A) at the end of the period is calculated as A = Principal + Simple Interest = P + (P × R × T / 100).

Relationship between SI and Rate

Simple Interest is directly proportional to Principal, Rate, and Time. If any of these double, the interest also doubles (keeping others constant).

SI vs CI for Year 1

For the first year (when compounded annually), Simple Interest and Compound Interest are always equal.
